title: Before, after, between

parent.why: Each step forward on the number line adds one, so the number after 6 is 6 + 1 = 7.
Stepping back one place takes one away, so the number before 6 is 5.

parent.learn: Between is the number in the middle.
parent.why: 5 and 7 have one number between them: 6, which is one after 5 and one before 7.

parent.learn: Count on from any number, not always from 1.
parent.why: Starting at 12 and saying “13, 14, 15” is faster than starting at 1 — and counting on is exactly how adding works later.
When the ones reach 9, one more fills a whole ten, so the tens go up by one and the ones start again at 0.

ask: Start at 12 and count on to 20.
Look at the calendar: today is the 14th — what will tomorrow be?
In the lift, which floor comes after 3?
I am thinking of the number just before 50. What is it?

rounds.h: After means one more: 3 and one more is 4.
Before means one less: one less than 5 is 4.
19 and one more fills the second ten: 20.
The 9 ones and one more make a new ten: 2 tens become 3 tens, so 30.
One less than 50 is 49: four tens and nine ones.
99 and one more makes ten tens, which is one hundred: 100.
Counting back takes one away each time: 23 − 1 = 22.
